title: Every new MOM contract must ship with its own Standby Spell or factory to prevent technical debt
content:
A.1.10.5.2.1.1 requires that "Each new MOM contract created must incorporate a Standby Spell or Standby Spell factory, which can be used to create new Standby Spells that can trigger the MOM contract," and gives the reason: "With a Standby Spell per every MOM contract, the generation of technical debt can be avoided."

This turns a discretionary optimization into a construction rule. Left optional, Standby Spells would be written reactively — after the first incident where their absence hurt — and coverage would be permanently uneven, with the newest and least-understood breakers being exactly the ones lacking a fast trigger.

Calling the gap "technical debt" is the interesting framing. A MOM contract without a Standby Spell is not missing a feature; it is a safety mechanism that silently fails its latency requirement. It appears complete in the codebase and only reveals the shortfall during the emergency it was built for.

The rule generalizes: where a capability's value depends on how fast it can be invoked, the invocation path is part of the capability, not an accessory to it.
description: Coupling the circuit breaker to its trigger at creation time stops the codebase accumulating breakers that cannot be fired quickly when they are actually needed.
